name: Parallel FX network: same input to up to three effects, heavy drive alongside clean delay, phase-flip a loop to cancel its dry and keep only wet, per-loop EQ/levels, effects inside the delay loop
goal: Turn a serial chain into a parallel effects network for synth/pad/lead layers: feed the same dry input to up to three effect loops and sum them (so a high-gain drive can growl in the background while a delay stays clean), use a per-loop phase invert to cancel the dry component of an effect without a wet-only mode (inverted dry + summed dry ≈ wet only), check for effects that already invert phase (chorus) against the dry, balance with per-loop EQ, send/return levels and master, and place an effect inside a delay's feedback/insert loop so repeats get processed — the portable parallel-distortion wet/dry recipe that was missing from the library.

source.title: Pedals in Parallel - Discovering new ways to use effects you thought you knew

prerequisites: Parallel mixer/bus with per-branch gain, phase invert and EQ (Web Audio: split to 3 GainNodes, sum; invert = gain −1; implementation note)
Drive/distortion, delay (ideally with insert/feedback loop), chorus/flanger, tremolo
constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
About three parallel branches is the practical maximum before phase issues become problems (a branch's internal dry/wet mix counts as another signal).
Some effects invert phase internally; in parallel with dry they partially cancel — always check the phase switch per branch.
Source demo is guitar pedals; signal-flow concepts are generic.

steps.action: Baseline: compare serial distortion→echo with echo→distortion to hear order-dependence.
Parallel: split the same dry input to drive and delay branches and sum. Keep drive high and sustaining in its branch while the delay branch handles clean repeats.
steps.expect: Growl under clean echoes — impossible in series

steps.action: Remove the dry from an effect that has no wet-only mode: flip the phase of that branch so its dry component cancels against the dry in the sum, leaving (mostly) the delay.
steps.expect: Wet-only repeats without a kill-dry switch

steps.action: Chorus = vibrato + dry: test phase flip on modulation effects; inverted dry won't fully 'unbake' into pure vibrato, and some pedals already invert phase, so pick the setting that sounds fuller.
Balance each branch with its EQ, send and return levels and a master volume; take the dry out entirely when only effects are wanted.
Insert loop: put another effect (e.g. modulation/space) inside the delay's insert/feedback path so delayed sound is processed again on each recirculation.
steps.expect: Repeats grow more spacious/distant each pass

steps.action: Swap in different trios of effects (e.g. delay + modulation + tremolo, envelope-controlled tremolo) to discover combinations.

verification: With phase flip on a full-mix delay branch, the summed output has noticeably less dry level.
Drive branch level can be raised without the delay repeats distorting.
Adding a fourth branch increases comb/phase artifacts (audible thinning).
